newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS - Iridium, telecom junk weakens.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS - Iridium, telecom junk weakens.

text.p: Iridium LLC junk bonds weakened on Monday, following news the company had lost contact with one of its satellites, traders said.
Meanwhile, junk bonds of competitive local exchange carriers slumped in reaction to a court ruling that overturned federal rules governing local telephone markets.
In broader markets, bids on junk bonds drifted lower by 1/4 to 3/8 of a point on Monday on very thin trading.
Spreads on investment-grade debt were unchanged on similarly sluggish trading volume, typical of a summer Monday.
Iridium units and bonds dropped one point each on news one of the five satellites launched by the company on July 9, prior to its first junk bond offering, was not properly functioning.
The company's units were quoted 97-99, while its 14 percent bonds were quoted 98-99.
Motorola Inc told Iridium that the scheduled date for commercial service should not be affected becuase it designed the IRIDUM system to accommodate such an anomaly.
Iridium and Motorola are building a satellite-based global telecommunications system.
In other news, Payless Cashways Inc, a building materials retailer, announced on Monday that it has filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy in order to facilitate a debt restructuring.
The news, which was largely anticipated by market players, pushed the company's bonds to 17-19 from an opening level of 24.
In the primary market, action continued to focus on junk bonds, with new issuance of investment-grade debt remaining muted.

Junk issuers to sell debt on Monday included Autotote Corp with a $110 million offering, Safety Components International Inc with a $90 million deal and State Brothers Holdings Inc with a $100 million deal.
In other markets, the Dow Jones Industrial Average ended the day higher by 16 points, stabilizing after Friday's 130-point drop.
Treasuries closed lower in a light session marked by scattered fears that Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan might deliver a hawkish message to Congress on Tuesday.
The price of the 30-year benchmark Treasury dropped 5/32 to close at 101-3/32, pushing its yield up to 6.54 percent.

Junk bonds of competitive local exchange carriers (CLECs) dropped 1/4 to 1/2 a point on Monday as the market reacted to a federal appeals court decision to overturn key parts of federal rules designed to pry open the $100 billion local telephone market controlled by regional Baby Bells.
Greg Froehlich, high-yield telecomm analyst at Merrill Lynch, said, "If it hurt the CLECs, it shouldn't have--it's another vote of confidence for facilities-based operators."
Froehlich said the ruling should not hurt high-yield CLEC issuers that have already built their own facilities and negotiated interconnection agreements with Baby Bells.
